results.explanation: The alleged authorization failure is refuted in the supplied source context. POST /process/text binds the caller through the verified-user dependency. When the caller supplies a collection name, the route validates that exact name with access_type='write' before constructing and saving the caller's text. For a non-admin, the shared policy checks an ordinary collection name as a possible knowledge-base ID and adds it to the allowed set only if the user has the requested access; the fallback allowance applies only when no knowledge base with that ID exists. Thus, for the declared existing knowledge base and a caller lacking ownership or an explicit write grant, the name remains denied, the validator raises HTTP 403, and the vector-database save is not reached. This matches the accepted expectation to deny.

entry.statement: The declared entry is POST /process/text, whose process_text handler receives form data and binds its runtime caller through get_verified_user.

binding.statement: The declared verified principal is bound to the handler's user value by Depends(get_verified_user), and that same user is supplied to collection-access validation.

control.statement: The caller-side validator passes the requested set and write access type to the shared accessibility filter, computes denied names, and raises HTTP 403 whenever any requested name is not allowed.

citations.quote:
async def _validate_collection_access(collection_names: list[str], user, access_type: str = 'read') -> None:
    """
    Raise 403 if the user lacks access to any of the requested collections.
    Delegates to the shared filter_accessible_collections utility so the
    access rules stay in one place.
    """
    requested = set(collection_names)
    allowed = await filter_accessible_collections(requested, user, access_type=access_type)
    denied = requested - allowed
    if denied:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN,
            detail=ERROR_MESSAGES.ACCESS_PROHIBITED,
        )

control.statement: For a non-admin targeting an existing knowledge-base ID, the strongest visible policy control admits the name only when Knowledges.check_access_by_user_id succeeds for the requested permission; if that check fails and the knowledge base exists, the name is not added to the allowed set.

control.statement: The special system meta-collection named knowledge-bases is a distinct checked resource and is always omitted for non-admins; the declared target is instead an existing individual knowledge-base collection handled by the ordinary-name branch.

effect.statement: The protected effect is saving a Document whose page content is the caller-supplied form content into the selected collection_name; this save occurs only after the supplied-name write validation completes.

condition.statement: The relevant request branch is the branch where the caller supplies collection_name; only a missing name is replaced by a content hash, while a supplied name is validated for write access.
The shared policy has a separate administrator bypass, so the declared non-admin proceeds through the per-collection checks rather than receiving unconditional access.

For an ordinary name, the policy distinguishes an existing knowledge-base ID from a nonexistent legacy or ephemeral collection: access is allowed upon the requested user permission, while the fallback applies only if no knowledge base exists.

scopeClaim.statement: This assessment is limited to the single declared runnable obligation and the supplied fixed source context; it makes no repository-wide or all-entry discovery claim.

relationCoverage.explanation: The source-visible decision is denial: the non-admin does not take the admin bypass, and an existing knowledge-base ID is allowed only if the user-specific write-access check succeeds. With the declared absence of write access, validation raises HTTP 403.

The save of caller-selected text is sequenced after write validation. Under the declared existing-KB/no-write-access branch, validation denies the name and raises before the save, so the protected effect is unreachable.
The entry requires a verified user, and a caller-supplied collection name triggers explicit write-access validation before processing reaches the vector-database save.

No source-external fact is needed to decide this declared branch. The obligation itself fixes that the target is an existing knowledge base and that the non-admin lacks write access; the source shows that the only permissive fallback in this branch is for a name that is not a knowledge base, which is excluded by those fixed conditions.

The handler obtains the runtime user through get_verified_user and passes that same user into the write-access validation, binding the declared verified non-admin principal to the identity evaluated by policy.

The caller-selected form_data.collection_name is the exact name submitted to write validation and later used by the save. The policy checks that ordinary name as a possible individual knowledge-base ID, distinct from the separately denied knowledge-bases system meta-collection.
